edges.mechanism: Arginine and lysine compete for cellular and intestinal transport (arginine-lysine antagonism); arginine undermines the HSV rationale for lysine, while excess lysine effects in rats were normalized by arginine. Deliberately co-administered in anxiety trials.
edges.evidence: Human tracer study (n=5), in vitro and rat data; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Lysine increased intestinal 47Ca absorption and blunted calciuria after a Ca load; lysine plus calcium strongly stimulated GLP-1 via CaSR in rats.
edges.evidence: Small human mechanistic study and rat study; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Lysine and aminoglycosides are each nephrotoxic at high doses in rats and toxicity was additive; lysine shares apical proximal-tubule uptake with gentamicin. No human data.
edges.evidence: Rat and cell studies; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Label mandates IV L-lysine/L-arginine (18-25 g each) to reduce renal radiation dose; amino-acid co-infusion causes metabolic acidosis and transient hyperkalemia. Oral supplements are not a substitute.
edges.evidence: FDA label, post-authorisation safety study (n=41), clinical series; moderate certainty for IV setting

edges.mechanism: Lysine acutely lowers postprandial glucose (-44% glucose AUC with glucose load; -9.1% at 60 min after mixed drink) and raises glucagon; no effect on insulin sensitivity in older adults.
edges.evidence: Acute crossover studies (n=7-13); no interaction study; low certainty

edges.mechanism: One RCT reported SBP falling from 146 to 129 mmHg with lysine in hypertensive adults; kidney-protective, diuretic effects in salt-sensitive rat model; possible additive BP lowering.
edges.evidence: Single small RCT plus animal/pilot human data; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Lysine and zinc are both proposed HSV symptomatic remedies; an open-label lysine/zinc/herbal product was associated with cold-sore resolution.
edges.evidence: Open-label pilot (n=30) and narrative review; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Ascorbate is a cofactor for lysyl hydroxylase, which converts collagen lysine to hydroxylysine; ascorbate raised lysyl hydroxylase activity 3-fold in fibroblasts.
edges.evidence: In vitro and review; mechanistic only

edges.mechanism: Lysine/hydroxylysine residues form collagen cross-links; collagen biosynthesis depends on lysine modification. No combined supplementation trial.
edges.evidence: Biochemical reviews; mechanistic only

edges.mechanism: Narrative review proposes combined lysine, calcium and vitamin D for muscle/bone in cereal-based diets; untested.
edges.evidence: Narrative review only; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Dietary lysine (1.5%) did not alter iron or copper bioavailability in rats; no human interaction expected.
edges.evidence: Rat study; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Human case of Fanconi syndrome and tubulointerstitial nephritis progressing to chronic renal failure after oral lysine; dose-related nephrotoxicity in rats.
edges.evidence: Case report and animal data; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Treatment is a low-lysine diet to limit neurotoxic glutaric/3-hydroxyglutaric acids; supplementation counteracts therapy.
edges.evidence: Evidence-based guideline and review; moderate certainty

edges.mechanism: Managed with lysine-restricted diet +/- arginine to reduce alpha-AASA/P6C; supplemental lysine opposes therapy.
edges.evidence: Cohort studies and review; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Inborn defect of lysine degradation; adding lysine raises an already elevated substrate.
edges.evidence: Systematic case review; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Low mealtime doses normalize plasma lysine without hyperammonemia, but 0.55-1.1 mmol/kg doses caused profuse diarrhea and IV loads occasionally raised ammonia; specialist use only.
edges.evidence: Cohort (n=27, 12 mo) and small studies; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Lysine(+methionine)-rich diets raised cholesterol in rabbits and lysine raised LDL-C on low-protein diets in rats; review advises caution in cardiovascular or gallbladder disease. 1 g/d had no lipid effect in humans.
edges.evidence: Animal data, review, one human RCT; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Adverse effects of excess lysine in rats (weight loss, lower albumin, higher LDL-C) were confined mainly to low-protein diets; excess intake can cause amino-acid imbalance.
edges.evidence: Rat study and review; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: No data on high-dose lysine during lactation; probably low risk, alternative may be preferred for newborn/preterm infants.
edges.evidence: LactMed monograph; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Supplemental lysine raises plasma lysine (~3-fold after a load) and plasma/urine 2-AAA, and shifts arginine/lysine ratios; can confound metabolomic biomarker interpretation (true physiological change, not assay artifact).
edges.evidence: Human acute studies; moderate certainty for direction

edges.mechanism: IV lysine/arginine causes metabolic acidosis and K+ rise (mean +0.60 mmol/L at 4 h); 75 g IV lysine produced K+ 6.3-6.8 mmol/L. Not shown with oral supplement doses.
edges.evidence: Clinical studies in radionuclide therapy; moderate certainty (IV only)
